samples.question: This image shows a pen drawn on white paper with one animal in it. The FENCE is the large loop of thick straight rails, all painted in the same single dark colour; it is the only barrier in the picture. The ANIMAL is the one solid round blob inside the loop. The pale elongated bars inside the pen are feeding troughs and the four short grey ticks at the corners of the page are fixed decoration: neither is a barrier, neither blocks movement, and both are drawn the same way whatever the answer is. A GAP is a stretch of one rail where no paint has been laid down, so the white paper runs straight through the line of the fence from the inside of the pen to the outside. There is at most one gap; it may sit anywhere along any rail, or there may be no gap at all. The animal counts as able to get out if it can travel from where it stands to the edge of the page without ever crossing painted fence; it may walk over troughs freely, and it does not matter how far it happens to be standing from the fence or from the gap. The shape and size of the pen, the number of rails, the thickness of the rails, the colours, the number of troughs, and where the animal stands all change from image to image and none of them tells you the answer. Judge only the fence you can actually see in this image, and do not assume that a pen drawn round an animal must be closed. Can the animal get out of the pen? Answer yes or no.
